keys.description: file holding the agent role's assertion key (at least 32 bytes). agent-api holds the same file; no other process does. Without it no agent request can be verified
file holding the human role's assertion key (at least 32 bytes). The terminal holds the same file; never agent-api, never a worker. Without it nobody can consent or store a credential

file holding the gateway's Ed25519 PUBLIC identity key (gateway-identity.v1, SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM) — the same file agent-api and meeting-api verify with. Every agent-role and git-role call must carry the gateway's X-Vexa-Identity naming the assertion's actor, forwarded unchanged by agent-api; without a valid one the call is refused, so the agent key alone cannot act for anybody. The broker verifies and cannot sign; a private key here refuses the boot
file holding the git role's assertion key. agent-api's Git credential store holds the same file when it is switched to the broker

the broker's private state directory: connection metadata and audit (metadata.sqlite), the encrypted local store (secrets.sqlite), and the generated key that derives PKCE verifiers. A persistent volume no other service mounts

credential store backend: `local` (AES-256-GCM in the state directory, keyed by VEXA_CONNECTIONS_STORE_KEY_FILE) or `openbao` (an OpenBao or Vault KV v2 mount the operator runs). Any other value refuses the boot (ADR-0040)

keys.default: (unset — required when VEXA_CONNECTIONS_STORE=local, and the boot refuses without it)
keys.description: file holding the local store's AES-256 key as 64 hex characters (`openssl rand -hex 32`). Mounted from a secret, never from the state volume, so a copied volume or backup is ciphertext only
base URL of the operator's OpenBao or Vault server: https://, or plain http:// only to a loopback address on this host (the boot refuses anything else)
file holding a token whose policy grants create, update and read on <mount>/data/*. Read on every request, so a renewed token file takes effect without a restart
the KV v2 mount the broker writes under
the Google OAuth client id Gmail and Calendar consent uses. Usually the same client the terminal signs in with (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)
the registered callback, exactly `<terminal public origin>/api/auth/callback/google` over https. The terminal routes `vxc_` states arriving there to the broker and leaves sign-in callbacks alone

google_oauth.description: Gmail and Google Calendar connections: the broker can start Google consent and exchange its code
google_oauth.when_unconfigured: authorizing a Gmail or Calendar connection answers 409 'Provider application is not configured on this deployment'; custom-secret connections are unaffected

git_store.description: agent-api's Git credential store may keep saved tokens and deploy keys in this broker
git_store.when_unconfigured: POST /api/internal/git-secret refuses every caller (403); agent-api keeps Git credentials in its own encrypted store
